# RUSTSEC-2026-0387

Crypto-bigint 0.5.5, timing variability
in operations meant to be constant-time. Dated 2026-10-23, and it
red-ed `security` on every runner PR, docs-only ones included (e.g.
#2274), without any change to Cargo.lock.

NOT UPGRADABLE FROM HERE. The fix is >= 0.7.6, a semver-MAJOR bump.
0.5.5 is the last 0.5 release, and every elliptic-curve 0.13.x
requires `crypto-bigint ^0.5`. crypto-bigint enters through exactly
one chain:

    qontinui-runner (default `restate` feature) -> restate-sdk 0.10
    -> restate-sdk-shared-core 0.10.0 (`request_identity`)
    -> jsonwebtoken 10.4.0 (`rust_crypto`) -> p256 0.13 / p384 0.13
    -> elliptic-curve 0.13.8 (directly, and via ecdsa / primeorder)
    -> crypto-bigint 0.5.5

No later release in that chain moves it, semver-major ones included.
As of 2026-10-24, every jsonwebtoken up to the latest, 11.1.0,
requires p256 ^0.13.2 and p384 ^0.13.0, and restate-sdk up to the
latest, 0.12.1, still takes jsonwebtoken ^10.3.

NOT REACHABLE. Only jsonwebtoken's ES256/ES384 code reaches it.
restate-sdk-shared-core's request_identity verifies EdDSA tokens and
nothing else (`Validation::new(Algorithm::EdDSA)`). That path uses
ed25519-dalek, which does not depend on crypto-bigint. Even that
check runs only when an identity key is set through the endpoint
builder's `.identity_key(..)`, and runner code never calls it. So no
p256/p384 operation runs. If one did, ECDSA verification works only
on public inputs (key, signature, message), and a timing leak
exposes only secret operands. The runner has no direct dependency on
jsonwebtoken, p256, p384 or elliptic-curve.

This ignore can go when jsonwebtoken ships on p256/p384 >= 0.14
(elliptic-curve 0.14 -> crypto-bigint 0.7) and restate-sdk adopts
that release. Moving restate-sdk to the `aws_lc_rs` backend with
default features off would also remove p256 from the graph. That
swaps the crypto backend, adds the aws-lc-rs C build, and means
re-listing the defaults the runner needs (`http_server`, for
`HttpServer::new` in src-tauri/src/restate/http_endpoint.rs). So
it is not done here. Re-assess immediately if the runner starts
signing with an ES256/ES384 key, or starts using a P-256/P-384
private key through elliptic-curve 0.13 anywhere.

Drop when jsonwebtoken ships on p256/p384 >= 0.14 (elliptic-curve 0.14 -> crypto-bigint 0.7) and restate-sdk adopts that release.
